PullRequest.Title: nes: Recognize eagerness option in PatchBased02Unified
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: PatchBased02Unified eagerness requests were misclassified, redundantly applying a generic debounce or minimum-response delay on every invocation and holding the first visible edit.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Inline edit suggestions could be artificially delayed to 700 ms at Medium aggressiveness or 1500 ms at Low aggressiveness before the first edit was shown.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The added strategy classification skips the redundant generic aggressiveness timing policy for PatchBased02Unified eagerness requests, allowing the HTTP request and first streamed edit to follow the strategy's baked latency settings rather than being held to the generic 700/1500 ms targets.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 548 introduced PatchBased02Unified. Its model configuration accepts eagernessPrompt and its prompt path emits an aggression tag, but before this change isEagernessPrompt omitted the strategy. Therefore xtabProvider._configureDebounceTimings invoked _applyAggressivenessSettings for each non-speculative inline-edit request. Low and Medium set DelaySession.expectedTotalTime to configured defaults of 1500 ms and 700 ms, and stream processing explicitly waits out the remaining artificial delay before yielding the first edit.

Scenarios.Scenario: A non-speculative next-edit request using PatchBased02Unified with eagernessPrompt enabled, especially when the user selects Medium or Low inline-edit aggressiveness.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Model configuration is resolved, _configureDebounceTimings runs, prompt/context is assembled, debounce completes, endpoint.makeChatRequest2 starts one streaming model request, and the first parsed edit may be delayed before it is yielded. Before the diff, misclassification set an expected total time and the first edit waited up to the remaining 700/1500 ms; after the diff that redundant wait is skipped. Background telemetry collection is off the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stream an inline-edit model response through endpoint.makeChatRequest2.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per surviving invocation, with only the pre-existing retry paths able to add another request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same model request was made, but Medium/Low generic aggressiveness timing could hold the first parsed edit until 700/1500 ms total elapsed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The network response feeds the first visible edit. The diff does not change request count; it removes the client-side artificial wait that could remain after tokens arrived.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve optional language context through registered context providers and ignored-resource checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one aggregate context-gathering pass per invocation when language context is enabled, over the already registered providers and returned snippets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same optional context pass existed; only the later generic artificial first-edit delay differed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the model request when enabled, bounded by the existing debounce-derived time budget. The changed predicate does not add providers or calls; with the unified strategy's baked zero debounce it does not create additional context time.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The mechanism occurs once per surviving non-speculative inline-edit invocation. Cost scales with interaction frequency rather than document size; every qualifying Medium/Low request could incur the configured minimum response target.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Context gathering is awaited and cancellation-aware before the model request. A surviving invocation issues one streaming network request; existing cancellation and retry behavior are unchanged. The diff changes neither parallelism nor request fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The predicate has no cache and changes no cache key or cache lifetime. PatchBased02Unified's existing cacheDelay and rebasedCacheDelay settings remain unchanged, so cold/warm suggestion-cache behavior is not altered by this diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed predicate directly gates _applyAggressivenessSettings; DelaySession and stream processing show the resulting per-request artificial delay on the visible-edit critical path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact prevalence depends on rollout of PatchBased02Unified with eagernessPrompt and user aggressiveness selection, but the 700/1500 ms defaults and the first-edit wait are explicit in code.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression is introduced. The diff fixes a concrete repeated-delay regression by recognizing the unified model as eagerness-aware; the fixing change was recorded for regression learning.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and the affected inline-edit request path. No actionable performance regression was introduced. The production change removes a redundant per-request latency policy for PatchBased02Unified, while network, context-provider, cache, retry, cancellation, and concurrency behavior remain unchanged.
